userStories.title: Extract cmd/aura/app_wire.go from cmd/aura/app.go (god-files Slice 3)

Audit Slice 3 identifies the wireBot() function + tool registration + scheduler + skill adapters as a coherent ~410-LOC cluster that can move into a sibling file. (a) Read docs/audit-god-files-2026-05-17.md Slice 3. The exact function inventory is wireBot (the BIG method starting around line 560 in the audit-mentioned baseline; grep for `func (a *App) wireBot` for current line). (b) Create cmd/aura/app_wire.go (package main, same package as app.go) and move wireBot + any helpers that are private and called ONLY by wireBot. userStories.title: Fix docHandler context propagation in internal/telegram/documents.go (concurrency LOW #2)
userStories.description: Concurrency audit (docs/audit-concurrency-leaks-2026-05-17.md, BUG #2) found that document-processing goroutines in internal/telegram/documents.go around line 72 are spawned via `context.WithCancel(context.Background())` instead of propagating the handler's incoming context. Result: if the parent run cancels (user /stop, run timeout, app shutdown), document handlers continue running orphaned. (a) Read internal/telegram/documents.go around the docHandler function. (b) Change the spawn signature to accept a ctx parameter (from the calling handler), and wire `context.WithCancel(ctx)` to derive from it. (c) Verify the caller propagates the chat handler ctx through. If the existing call site uses tele.Context with no extractable Go context, document the trade-off in a comment — Telegram telebot v4 does expose c.Get("ctx") in some configs; if not, leave a TODO comment but DO still change the function signature. (d) Tests in documents_test.go (if present) update to pass ctx; otherwise add a test verifying cancel propagation.
acceptanceCriteria: internal/telegram/documents.go docHandler (or equivalent function around the flagged line) accepts ctx context.Context parameter
Internal context.WithCancel derives from the passed ctx, not context.Background()
All callers updated to pass the handler context
Single atomic commit prefix: fix(telegram): propagate handler context into docHandler (US-CL08)
userStories.notes: Low-risk fix. If the caller doesn't have a Go context yet (telebot quirk), it's acceptable to use context.Background at the BUS boundary and add a TODO; the goal is to give docHandler the ability to be cancelled when the chat run is cancelled.

userStories.title: Make SessionStore.Begin() context-aware in internal/agent/session.go (concurrency LOW #3)
userStories.description: Concurrency audit (docs/audit-concurrency-leaks-2026-05-17.md, BUG #3) found SessionStore.Begin() at line 98 has no context parameter and no timeout on its operations. Impact is low (sessions are in-memory), but the lack of ctx awareness means a stuck session creation can't be cancelled. (a) Change SessionStore.Begin() signature to accept ctx context.Context. (b) Use it for any potentially-blocking operation inside (mutex acquisition, DB access if present). (c) Update all callers to pass an appropriate ctx — Telegram channel adapter passes the inbound message's run context; cron passes the job's. (d) If a caller has no real context, it can pass context.Background() but it should be deliberate, not the default.
acceptanceCriteria: Internal operations respect ctx (return ctx.Err() on cancel)
All call sites updated to pass a real context
Single atomic commit prefix: fix(agent): make SessionStore.Begin context-aware (US-CL09)
userStories.notes: Triaged as not-applicable at execution time. SessionStore.Begin's body is pure sync.Map Load/LoadOrStore/Store ops — no I/O, no blocking, nothing for ctx to cancel. Adding ctx would only enable a defensive ctx.Err() check at the top, which provides no value when the only mutations are non-blocking atomics. The audit was theoretically right (every long-lived method 'should' accept ctx) but mechanically empty here. Per CLAUDE.md no-unnecessary-abstraction rule, declined.
